### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19 appeared in about 55 in 100 traces (110 of 200) and A20 in about 45 in 100 (91 of 200), with essentially every trace containing exactly one of the two and almost never both; in the later window, A19 appears in about 1 in 200 traces, A20 in about 4 in 200, and about 97.5 in 100 traces contain neither. [OCC001, OCC002, REL001]
- The routing out of A40 changed almost completely: before, its outgoing transitions led to A19 in about 50 in 100 cases and to A20 in about 43 in 100; in the later window, about 93 in 100 lead directly to A25, with A19 and A20 nearly gone as successors. [DIR002]
- The ordering ties around the two activities disappeared: before, A40 preceded A19 in about 55 in 100 traces and A19 preceded A25 in about 55 in 100, while A40 preceded A20 in about 45 in 100 and A20 preceded A25 in about 45 in 100; in the later window, A25 occurs without A19 in about 99.5 in 100 traces and without A20 in about 98 in 100. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]
- The gap between A40 and A25 shrank: before, A25 typically followed A40 two positions later (about 92 in 100 observations), consistent with one activity sitting in between; in the later window it typically follows immediately (about 93 in 100). [LAG002]
- The few remaining occurrences are too sparse to characterise: A20's outgoing transitions in the later window rest on 4 observations (A25 in half, A09 and A27 once each), the A40–A20 gap on 3 observations, and A19's position on a single occurrence; the position indicators mainly mirror the frequency collapse rather than a shift in where the activities occur. [DIR001, LAG001, POS001, POS002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the intermediate step between A40 and A25 — previously an either/or execution of A19 (in roughly 55 in 100 traces) or A20 (in roughly 45 in 100) — is no longer executed, so that in the later window A40 is directly followed by A25. The signs are direct and mutually consistent: participation in A19 and A20 collapsed, A40's outgoing transitions now go to A25 in about 93 in 100 cases, the A40-to-A25 distance shrank from typically two positions to one, and the ordering relations A40-before-A19/A20-before-A25 vanished while A25 and A40 themselves still appear in essentially every trace. Thirteen items were flagged against roughly 0.48 expected by chance at these thresholds, and every difference exceeds those seen in about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled traces. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, LAG001, LAG002]

Limitations remain: most flagged items describe the same underlying behaviour — the near-disappearance of A19 and A20 — so they are not independent confirmations, and the behaviour of the few remaining occurrences rests on only 1–4 observations. The windows are finite samples of 200 traces each, so sampling differences in variant frequencies cannot be fully ruled out, although a fall from about 110 to 1 traces for A19 is far beyond what random re-splits typically produce. Zero participation in the later window shows only that A19 and A20 were not observed there, not that they are absent from the process. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, LAG001, POS001, POS002]
